# dnsrace 0.7.0

dnsrace 0.7.0 makes the app aware of the DNS servers your machine is actually using, adds eight
themes, and turns the results table into a faster tool for comparing and applying resolvers. It is
built and tested with Rust 1.99.1.

## Highlights

- **Automatic DNS detection on every platform.** dnsrace now reads the active resolver
  configuration at startup and on demand, shows the interface and detection source, and labels
  known addresses with their provider name (for example `1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare)`).
- **Refresh detection and Test current DNS.** Detect again after switching networks, copy the
  current addresses, or benchmark exactly the resolvers this machine is using.
- **Eight themes.** System, Dark, Light, Midnight, Nord, Solarized Light, Dracula and High
  contrast. `System` follows the operating system's light/dark preference.
- **A more useful results table.** Sort by provider, server, cached/uncached latency, score,
  DNSSEC or health; reverse the order; filter by health and category.
- **Compare with what you have.** The recommendation card marks the winner as already in use and
  explains which current DNS servers an apply would replace.
- **Safer exports.** Report filenames no longer overwrite an export made in the same second.

## Added

- **Cross-platform DNS auto-detection.**
  - Linux: `systemd-resolved` per-link data, the active NetworkManager connection, the default
    route/interface, `/etc/resolv.conf` and systemd-resolved's upstream resolver file.
  - Windows: `Get-NetIPConfiguration` through PowerShell, with a `pwsh` fallback and a
    language-independent registry fallback (`NameServer` / `DhcpNameServer`).
  - macOS: `scutil --dns`, `networksetup` service order and DNS values, plus the default route.
- **Detection details in the interface:** active interface, gateway, source description and
  provider names for known current DNS addresses.
- **Refresh detection** in the toolbar and sidebar, plus **Test current DNS** and **Copy**.
- **Theme presets:** System, Dark, Light, Midnight, Nord, Solarized Light, Dracula and High
  contrast, available in Settings and from a quick picker in the toolbar.
- **Sortable column headings** with ascending/descending order, including Provider, Server,
  Cached, Uncached, Score, DNSSEC and Health.
- **Result filters** for health state and resolver category, in addition to the existing text
  search.
- **Current-DNS comparison** in the recommendation card, including an `IN USE` badge and the
  addresses an apply will replace.
- **Keyboard shortcuts:** Ctrl/Cmd+R or F5 refreshes detection, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter tests selected,
  Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Enter tests all, Ctrl/Cmd+E exports HTML and Esc cancels a run.
- **History metadata:** saved runs now keep the scanned and tested counts, and old history files
  still load with sensible defaults.
- **Main-branch snapshot workflow:** every push to `main` builds downloadable Linux, Windows and
  macOS artifacts in addition to the normal CI checks.
- **Release validation:** the release workflow now checks that the tag matches `Cargo.toml` and
  that the matching release-notes file exists before building anything.

## Changed

- **Startup no longer blocks on detection.** System detection runs on a background thread, so the
  window opens immediately even when a platform command is slow or missing.
- **Provider-aware current DNS text** is used in the toolbar, sidebar, recommendation, clipboard
  summary, JSON details and HTML report.
- **The recommendation card** shows whether the chosen resolver is already configured and what it
  would replace.
- **Theme handling** now applies a full palette (background, panels, borders, hover, selection and
  text) instead of only switching egui's dark/light base style.
- **The HTML report only includes a Steering section when steering was actually checked.**
- **JSON reports add `current_dns_details`** with the IP, provider and a `known_provider` flag;
  the stable `current_dns` address list is unchanged.
- **History labels and the History window** show how many resolvers were tested.
- **Rust toolchain is pinned to 1.99.1** through `rust-toolchain.toml`, and the CI/release
  workflows use the same version.
- **GitHub Actions were refreshed** (`checkout@v5`, current artifact actions, release concurrency
  and tag validation).

## Fixed

- **0.6.0 did not compile with current `rustls-native-certs`.** The 0.8 API returns a
  `CertificateResult`; dnsrace now uses its certificate list correctly.
- **DNS replies are validated against the question that was sent.** A reply with the right
  transaction ID but a different name, type or class is rejected instead of being measured.
- **DoH now supports every query type and DNSSEC checks.** The DoH path previously could not carry
  the DNSSEC and AAAA probes used by the full test.
- **A panicked full-test task no longer freezes progress.** Finished tasks that cannot produce a
  row still advance the progress counter.
- **NetworkManager names containing escaped colons** are parsed correctly.
- **The current-DNS display and `IN USE` badge update after Apply or Revert**, so they never keep
  describing the resolver configuration that was just replaced.
- **Platform command output is decoded lossily**, so a localized or non-UTF-8 Windows adapter name
  cannot discard the detected DNS addresses.
- **System candidates are only added to plain-DNS runs**, so a DoH run no longer wastes time on
  plain IP candidates that cannot answer over DoH.
- **Exports made within the same second** get a numeric suffix instead of overwriting the previous
  file.
- **The GUI no longer performs blocking detection in the constructor**, which could delay the first
  frame on systems where a detection command hangs.

## Updated

- Version: **0.7.0**.
- Minimum and tested Rust: **1.99.1**.
- README, AppStream metadata and release notes for 0.7.0.
- CI and release workflows for Rust 1.99.1, with a separate `main` snapshot workflow.

## Downloads

| Platform | File |
| --- | --- |
| Linux x86_64 | `dnsrace-0.7.0-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux aarch64 | `dnsrace-0.7.0-aarch64.AppImage` |
| Windows x86_64 | `dnsrace-0.7.0-windows-x86_64.zip` |
| macOS Intel | `dnsrace-0.7.0-macos-x86_64.zip` |
| macOS Apple silicon | `dnsrace-0.7.0-macos-aarch64.zip` |

Every release includes `SHA256SUMS.txt`; AppImages also have individual `.sha256` files.

### Linux

```sh
chmod +x dnsrace-0.7.0-x86_64.AppImage
./dnsrace-0.7.0-x86_64.AppImage
```

If FUSE is unavailable, use `--appimage-extract-and-run`. Applying DNS uses NetworkManager or
`resolvectl`; the app asks for elevated privileges only when needed.

### Windows

Unzip the archive and run `dnsrace.exe`. Applying DNS opens a UAC prompt because it changes the
active adapter's resolver settings.

### macOS

Unzip the archive and move `dnsrace.app` to Applications. The app is unsigned, so the first launch
may require right-clicking it and choosing **Open**, or running:

```sh
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine dnsrace.app
```

Applying DNS asks for administrator approval and saves the previous settings for **Revert**.

## Verification

- 98 unit tests and 9 engine integration tests pass.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` are clean.
- `cargo build --release --locked` succeeds on Rust 1.99.1.
- The Linux AppImage is built, extracted and validated with `desktop-file-validate` and
  `appstreamcli` in the release workflow.

## Notes

- Only plain DNS resolvers on port 53 can be applied as the system resolver. DoT and DoH entries
  remain benchmark-only.
- dnsrace makes no telemetry requests. It contacts the resolver endpoints you test and Cloudflare's
  1.1.1.1 for the DNS CHAOS edge lookup. Cloudflare's HTTPS trace endpoint and public-dns.info are
  contacted only when the optional nearby-country list is enabled.
- See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Yousef-Mohamed22/dnsrace/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the
  full list of changes.
